I want to disclose that my brother-in-law works for the Department for the Aging, and I'd like permission to explain my vote. (PAUSE)

Thank you. As the chair of the Committee on Civil Service and Labor, I am excited to vote yes for 692-A. Paraprofessionals are vital to public

education. Council Member De La Rosa's bill takes a significant first step towards fixing the persistent paraprofessional staffing crisis that has been impacting New York City schools. Paraprofessionals are critical members of our school environment, providing instructional, behavioral, and physical support to students with disabilities. This is an important first step towards recognizing the true value of our city's paraprofessionals. Providing them with some reprieve and incentivizing recruitment and retention. Just want to be very clear, I have a deep respect for the collective bargaining process. This bill's non-pensionable workforce stabilization payment structure does not interfere, in my view, with mandatory subjects of collective bargaining, as it does not attempt to legislate wages or benefits and matters that must be resolved at the bargaining table. Congratulations to my colleague, Council Member Carmen De La Rosa, for her leadership on this

bill and for her dedication to our city's paraprofessionals and the students and families who depend on them. And thank you, Speaker Menin, for moving this bill to the floor to vote on today. I vote yes on all.

I vote aye, with the exception of Intro 972 and Intro 983-A. I also echo the sentiments of Council Member Aldebol, and I would like to see the same collectiveness for our EMS workers. I should have done this first, Majority Leader. I'm sorry, I disclose that my son works for the DSNY. Thank you.
Thank you, Council Member. Council Member Avilés? COUNCIL MEMBER AVILÉS: I'd like to disclose for the record that my daughter is a student at New York City Public Schools. I vote aye on all.

I would like to disclose first that I have a brother who works for the New York City Parks Department, as well as a brother who works for the Department of Juvenile Justice. First of all, thank you, Majority Leader. And first, I want to again thank the Speaker and my good, good colleague, Council Member Carmen De La Rosa, for ushering this particular bill, the Paraprofessional Workforce Stabilization Bill, forth. This particular bill is extremely important, as the Council Member from the 42nd Council District, I've had the opportunity to sit down with paraprofessionals from schools throughout my community, and I've heard about the long hours and the dedication they bring to the classrooms, and the sacrifices they make to support our students while working to support their own families.

These are hardworking New Yorkers paying rent or a mortgage, they're buying groceries, paying for childcare, doing everyday things that help build this city and make it bigger, brighter, and better. They are everyday New Yorkers who walk into our schools ready to support our children who need a little extra patience, encouragement, and care. They celebrate our students' successes, help them overcome challenges, and often become some of the most trusted adults in their lives. That's why this bill matters. It sends a clear message that the City values the work of our paraprofessionals who do big, amazing jobs every day. When we invest in our paraprofessionals, we're investing in our students and our schools and our communities. And let me be clear, this legislation does not replace or weaken the collective bargaining process. It is not a substitute for the work that happens at the bargaining table. This is a one-time payment that recognizes the extraordinary commitment of our paraprofessionals while those broader

conversations continue. have a responsibility to look out for the people who look out for our children, and today we have the opportunity to do just that. I'm proud to support Intro 692, and I hope to see it-- it will cross the finish line today (TIMER) because our paraprofessionals have earned more than our gratitude. Let's continue as we do today to put some respect on that check. Thank you.
Council Member Avilés? COUNCIL MEMBER AVILÉS: Yes, I forgot to mention, uh, to disclose on the record that my sister works for the Parks Department, thank you.

I vote aye. I teach

at CUNY, and I do want to thank the commission that looked the pay salaries, particularly Carl Weisbrod, Dr. Lillian Paoli-Barrios (sic) (*Barrios - Paoli), and Dr. Larian Angelo. They really are the best of New York in terms of their knowledge and city experience, and I want to thank them. (PAUSE)
I said, aye. I work and vote, and hang out at CUNY. I was very clear...
I got it, I got it. Thank you very much. Council Member Brooks-Powers?

I just want to echo the sentiments of my colleagues in terms of my deep, deep pleasure in being able to cast a vote for Intro 692-A. As a proud auntie of an autistic miracle

child, who depends on paraprofessionals each day, I've been able to see firsthand just how critical they are to the nurturing and development of our most valued gems in our lives, and that's our children. And so while, as has been said, this is a first step, I'm so thankful that we are serving in a body that is putting people first in terms of attacking the affordability issue and making sure people have wages or funding to be able to have a better quality of life. And so I commend the bill sponsor, Council Member De La Rosa, the Chair for Labor, as well as the Speaker for moving this forward. And with that, I vote aye on all. Thank you.
Council Member Cabán? COUNCIL MEMBER CABÁN: I vote aye on all, with the exception of Intro 913, on which I vote no. Thank you.
Thank you. Council Member De La Rosa?
A moment to explain my vote?

Thank you. One moment for 511 West 171st Street. I just want to say I strongly support this application. It will create cooperative home ownership for existing tenants of a building that has been working really hard to make sure that they can uplift this building and own their apartments. They'll be able to buy their apartments for $250.00. So that is building generational wealth. And the vacant apartments will sell at 80% AMI. And so that is what it means to truly keep communities together and to be able to build generational wealth and equity in communities. In terms of 692-A, I want to thank Speaker Menin for her leadership and her vision and for staying true throughout this process. I want to thank the UFT for their strong support, the paras who have led this work, obviously Chair Aldebol for her leadership, Chair Dinowitz for his leadership, and everyone else who was a part of making sure we could get here today. Shoutout to Assemblymember Keith

Powers, who was the original OG introducer of this bill. I want to talk about the numbers real quick—$32,000 a year is insufficient. After 15 years, they make $54,000 a year in the most expensive city in the country . With $1.5 billion on Carter cases, this bill will provide $10,000 in a one-time stabilization payment so that we can retain this workforce. There are 25,000 paraprofessionals in New York City helping the most vulnerable children. And right now, there are from 1,600 to 3,000 vacancies in this workforce. And finally, to the 47 council members who have signed on to this bill, thank you for your support. We have the Manhattan, the Bronx, and the Queens borough presidents. It's not too late for Staten Island. Come on over. As well as the other four council members. We have solid support for this legislation because we recognize that this is an equity issue. Workers in our city must not be facing eviction and having to pick up food at a food pantry (TIMER) when

they're helping our most vulnerable New Yorkers. So thank you all for the support.
Council Member, do you also have disclosers by any chance?
Do you have disclosures to make today?
No disclosures, and I vote aye on all.

I’d like to disclose on the record that we're funding CUNY in the transparency resolution, and while I don't hang out too much at Hunter, like Gale does, I am affiliated with that institution. Permission to explain my vote?

Thank you, Mr. Majority Leader. I want to thank Council Member De La Rosa, Speaker Menin, and Chair Aldebol for moving the para legislation forward.

You know, being in a classroom with students with disabilities, the people who care most, oftentimes for the most vulnerable students, are our paraprofessionals. You know, the ones who are there day in and day out for the kids who have the most significant needs are the ones with paraprofessionals. And they do just such incredible work. And I would always say thank you, right? Because that's what we can do. But as a city council member, we don't just have to say thank you. We can demonstrate our gratitude. And today we demonstrate that gratitude through this legislation, through the Respect Check, through recognizing the dignity in their work, through recognizing their work, and addressing-- beginning to address the inequities in the pay they receive. And as elected officials, we talk all the time about supporting our students. But we cannot support our students without supporting the people who do the work. We have to support the people who support our students in the classroom. Those are our

paraprofessionals. I am an emphatic yes on this legislation, on all pieces of legislation on today's agenda. And I once again want to thank Council Member De La Rosa, Chair Aldebol, and of course, Speaker Menin for really moving forward this really critical piece of legislation for our paras and for our students.
Thank you. Council Member Encarnación? DEPUTY WHIP ENCARNACIÓN: I vote aye on all.

Thank you, Majority Leader. I also want to thank Council Member De La Rosa, our Speaker, and Chair Aldebol. You think about it, you know, I went to public school, my kids went to public school, and in

those classes, the paraprofessionals changed lives. I know for my kids who struggled with learning disabilities, the paras were critical to their education. And to say to New Yorkers that you can live on $32,000 a year is beyond belief. No one here, no one in this city, thinks anyone who lives in any of our districts can survive in this great city of ours on $32,000. This is a small step in the direction to say to the paras and to the UFT that we see you, that we care about you, and we want you to stay in this profession. The idea that we either have 1,600 or 3,000 vacancies because people can't afford to take these jobs just continues to mean that we're spending more money somewhere else. This is a wise investment in our city, a wise investment in our paraprofessionals, and a wise investment in our future. I really want to applaud us all for taking this stance today. I want to applaud us all for taking the leadership, of course, with Speaker Menin

leading all the way, Carmen De La Rosa, and my Assemblymember, Keith Powers, that we wouldn't be here today without them and the powers who stand up every day. I vote aye. Also, just one last message about the salary increase. I think it's, you know, we need to make sure that leaders in our city want these jobs, and salaries that we get paid are below even nonprofit salaries. Like, I got paid, when I was a nonprofit leader, I got paid more than 10 years ago than I get paid today. And if we really want these people in our profession to make our city better, we need to do it by understanding that salaries mean something to people doing these jobs. I really applaud the Commission and the work we did and what we're doing today on that vote. Thank you.
Council Member Farías? COUNCIL MEMBER FARÍAS: I proudly vote aye on all.
I vote aye on all; no on Intro 972.

Proud to vote aye on all. I'm especially proud to support Intro 913-A by Council Member Farías-- Intro 913-A, which would raise the age limit for those who would like to take the civil service exam to become a police officer. Our police department plays an essential role in the issue of public safety, and we must ensure that they have the tools to be able to successfully carry out their important mission. Now, we've made progress on the issue of police headcount. We've made progress by removing barriers that get in the way of those who want to serve our city as a police officer. We've made progress, and there's still room to take the progress even further.

This legislation will allow us to do exactly that by expanding the pool of candidates allowed to take the required exams. I'm proud to vote aye on all, including 913-A. And also, congratulations, Carmen De La Rosa, on your bill as well. Thank you.
I vote aye on all. And ask for unanimous consent to vote on Land Use Call-ups. (PAUSE)
Thank you. Council Member Gutiérrez? COUNCIL MEMBER GUTIÉRREZ: Aye on all.

I just want to say, very, very briefly, especially to our paras: this is a proud moment and congratulations to you all, because the work that you do is vital to our school communities. And I'm going just to reiterate what I said in Committee, as one of the only council members who is just a little over 10 years removed from high school, I think she got me beat just a little bit, just a little bit. (LAUGHTER)

I want to just shoutout some of the paras that, you know, though I wasn't their student, they became like family to me. Ms. Barnes, Ms. Vee, Ms. Cookie, and my constituent, Ms. Talia (phonetic), who called me almost every day about this bill. This is what you deserve. And I can't wait for not just this, but for more things to come. I vote aye on all.

Thank you, Majority Leader. The North Shore of Staten Island is changing, and with that change comes a responsibility to make sure that we're approving projects that invest in the future of homes and the future of careers where families can thrive. And that is why I'm proud to be voting on two major projects that will be voted on today: The new Curtis High School expansion will— excuse me, the new Curtis High School that will expand the school's state-of-the-art nursing program. This 800-seat expansion will open the doors for more students to pursue a strong non-AI career pathway in healthcare, one of our borough's largest employment sectors. And second, I am proud to be voting in support of 198-208 Richmond Terrace, which will bring

107 new apartments, including 30 permanently affordable workforce housing units, to the transit-rich location in Saint George. I also want to say that my mother started as a paraprofessional, and I am very proud to be supporting our paraprofessionals today and the folks who helped make that happen. So thank you to our Speaker and the teams that made this happen. I vote aye on all. Thank you, Majority Leader.
Aye on all. I'd like to disclose for the record that I'm associated with the Brooklyn Museum.
Aye on all. And I'd like to disclose on the record, my son is a student in New York City Public Schools that we are funding, and my son works as a para. Thank you.
Yes. I would like to disclose that my children are students at the Department of Education, and we are funding them in this Stated Meeting today, uh, and with that, I vote aye on all.
I’d like to disclose that my kids are students in the New York Public Schools, which we are funding, and I vote aye on all. Thank you.

Thank you, Mr. Majority Leader. I want to take a moment to support Intro 692 today, which provides workforce stabilization payments for our school paraprofessionals. For far too long, paraprofessionals have been the backbone of our public schools without receiving the recognition or compensation that reflects the essential role that they play every single day. They support students with disabilities, assist teachers in managing classrooms, and provide individualized attention to children who need it the most. As we continue to face staffing shortages across our education system, retaining experienced paraprofessionals is critical. These workforce stabilization payments acknowledge the invaluable work paraprofessionals perform and represent an important step towards building a stronger and more equitable education system for our students and families.

I want to thank the UFT for their advocacy, Speaker Menin, and Council Member De La Rosa for advancing this legislation. I vote aye on all. And I would like to disclose for the record that my brother works for the MTA. Thank you.
Thank you. Council Member De La Rosa?
Apologies. I would like to disclose for the record that my daughter is a student at New York City Public Schools.

Thank you, Majority Leader. First, I want to disclose for the record that my mother is a teacher at Hunter. I vote aye on all.

And I'm especially proud to co-sponsor and vote yes on Intro 692, which recognizes the critical role that our school paraprofessionals play in supporting students across the city. The Para Respect Check is an important step forward towards providing paraprofessionals with the dignity, compensation, and respect they deserve. I'm also excited to vote for Intro 955, which makes it easier and faster for New Yorkers to open a small business. I urge my colleagues to sign on to a similar bill, Intro 875, the Stop Clock Bill, which focuses on transparency and accountability on permit timelines. Lastly, I want to recognize several of our summer interns: Dylan Miglio, Jade Acker, and Nathan Zellizer, who are about to complete their time with our office. Jade, Nathan, and Dylan, thank you for all your help, your service to the city, and I wish you every success... (CROSS-TALK)
